1st Corps Commander-level India-China talks in eastern sector held over 2 days: MEA; says ties gradually moving in positive direction
Just 1% of asylum seekers in UK genuine, insider says, as UN blasts Britain for allowing bogus claims
Antarctica gained 695 billion tons in 2021-23 as tropical warmth drove heavy snowfall
stories.summary: Between 2021 and 2023, Antarctica experienced a notable gain in ice mass, primarily driven by exceptional snowfall in East Antarctica. This unusual occurrence, influenced by warmer tropical ocean temperatures, caused atmospheric disturbances that transported moisture southward. Although this gain temporarily countered ongoing ice loss in other regions, it does not signify a change in Antarctica's long-term trend of declining ice mass.

stories.title: AI predicts fusion plasma instability 200 ms early, stops it in time
Artist puts Kashmiri poet Lal Ded's mysticism on Pashmina
Ladakh's tourist footfall continues rising; August sees most foreign visitors
Canadian couple donate 187-acre Ontario island sanctuary after protecting its wildlife for 36 years
stories.summary: Jim and Anne Purvis bought 187.4 acres on Ontario’s Wilson Island in 1989 and spent 36 years protecting the land as a family sanctuary. They have now donated the property to the Northumberland Land Trust, ensuring its forests, wetlands, grasslands and habitats for species at risk remain protected as a permanent nature reserve.

stories.title: Village head's appeal drove Ladakh LG's initiative to tap 90 million litres of glacial water for irrigation
NCPCR summons Meta India head over alleged child abuse ads
stories.summary: The NCPCR has summoned Meta India's managing director regarding ads linked to child exploitation. This action follows a BBC Eye report and a formal inquiry into Meta's systems. The commission will examine Meta India's role in the s' appearance. The inquiry considers stringent provisions under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. Meta stated it has zero tolerance for child exploitation and removed many suspicious accounts.

stories.title: Kharge ‘purification’ row escalates as Congress MPs demand FIR from Delhi Police
US Democrat urges House Speaker to sue Trump admin over triumphal arch, says Congress never approved funds
Meet Rachel Chen, 18, who won $100K for her breakthrough quantum math research using simple diagrams
stories.summary: Rachel Chen, an 18-year-old Los Angeles student, won $100,000 at the Regeneron Science Talent Search for expanding a 1997 mathematical idea involving Temperley-Lieb diagrams. Her research offers a visual way to describe complex quantum particle systems and spin representations, potentially helping researchers better understand connections between different quantum-mechanical states.

stories.title: Sri Lanka a close friend, India stands with it through thick and thin: Rajnath Singh
NHRC seeks report on hostel facilities for DU students from Delhi chief secretary, UGC
Expelled Bihar Congress functionaries protest outside party office, seek meeting with Rahul
In 1973, Montana released a gall fly to control spotted knapweed; decades later...
stories.summary: Controlling invasive spotted knapweed biologically has initiated an unexpected ecological chain reaction. Gall flies, introduced as a control measure, have turned into a vital winter food source for deer mice, causing a surge in their populations and an uptick in hantavirus spread. Areas dense with knapweed report more infected mice than those with native grasslands.

stories.title: She bought a Maine island to stop clear-cutting; 90 years after Audubon opened its first camp there
stories.summary: Hog Island Audubon Camp marks an impressive ninety years of promoting environmental education and research. Located in Maine, this island was rescued from deforestation by environmentalists Millicent Todd Bingham and Mabel Loomis Todd. The camp is also the birthplace of Project Puffin, which successfully revitalized seabird numbers. Today, it remains a vital training ground for future scientists, educators, and artists, with its influence extending to bird conservation throughout North America.

stories.title: Former Delhi chief secretary Rakesh Mehta found hanging at Noida residence, dies by suicide
Lindsay Clancy murder case: Lawyer asks Trump to pardon Massachusetts mother after mistrial
Scientists seeded clouds over China’s Muz Taw Glacier; fresh snow cut ice loss by 14% to 17%
stories.summary: Scientists tested cloud seeding over China’s Muz Taw Glacier in 2018 to create artificial snowfall and slow ice loss. The experiment used silver iodide generators to encourage snow formation. Researchers found that fresh snow made the glacier surface brighter and reduced the amount of ice lost over a short period. However, they said the results are preliminary and need further testing.

stories.title: Andrew Flintoff lists his £6.75 million Cheshire mansion, bought from Phil Neville in 2021
stories.summary: England cricket legend Andrew Flintoff has put his £6.75 million Cheshire mansion on the market, four years after his life-changing Top Gear car crash. Bought from former Manchester United star Phil Neville in 2021, the 10,000 sq ft luxury property features six bedrooms, six bathrooms, four floors, a pool, gym, cinema and games room.

stories.title: Inside a $29M California mansion no one has ever lived in
stories.summary: A French-style manor in Rancho Santa Fe is now for sale at $29 million. This newly built home features antique materials and custom artisan craftsmanship throughout. The expansive residence includes a main house and a separate guest house on 3.66 acres. It boasts a zero-edge pool, gardens, and breathtaking views from its terraces. The manor comes fully furnished with art and antiques, ready for immediate occupancy.

stories.title: Meet Anvith, Dubai student who watched his brother’s school commute and built a free carpool service
stories.summary: In a bid to tackle traffic congestion, a student from Dubai has launched a unique carpooling website that connects commuters with similar routes through sophisticated algorithmic matching. Community Carpool now boasts over a thousand registered users in Dubai, ensuring user privacy by discreetly matching individuals until they agree to share rides. Notably, a local property developer has embraced this platform for its workforce, facilitating its growth.

stories.title: An 81-year-old US homeowner faced a $17,827.96 lien after a burst-pipe insurance claim was denied
stories.summary: Tyler Perry has made headlines with his philanthropic intervention for an elderly homeowner in Illinois. With her insurance company, Allstate, refusing to cover the damages from burst pipes, she faced the threat of foreclosure. Perry's willingness to pay off a significant property lien and provide additional financial support has saved her from losing her home and brightened her future.

stories.title: Twin girls once given less than 10% chance of survival are now ready for their first day of school
stories.summary: Ruby and Scarlett were given less than a 10% chance of survival after being diagnosed with Twin-to-Twin Transfusion Syndrome at 16 weeks. Following high-risk surgery, premature birth and serious health complications, the twins spent 300 days in hospital. Now, their mother Hanna Brameld is celebrating as her daughters prepare for their first day of school.

stories.title: In 2023, an Australian cattle station sold for $40 million for a carbon project; three years later...
stories.summary: After a disappointing turn of events, Benmara Station, a prominent cattle property in Australia, was sold for A$26 million, significantly lower than its original price of A$40 million. This decline resulted from the cancellation of an ambitious environmental project related to carbon farming, emphasizing traditional pastoral values instead of its former carbon potential as regulatory challenges mounted.

stories.title: Does AfD's big win in Germany signal a 'far right' uprising in Europe?
stories.summary: Many years ago, Otto von Bismarck observed that politics was “the art of the possible”. The modern European establishment appears to have inverted the Iron Chancellor’s maxim. Politics has increasingly become the art of explaining to voters why what they want is impossible, irresponsible, xenophobic, Islamophobic, nativist or, inevitably, far right. And made it impossible to vote for the so-called far-right party that’s actually willing to admit there’s a problem.

stories.title: Satya Niketan building collapse: MCD crackdown begins across Delhi; 24 properties demolished, 7 sealed
Kentfield Home Hits Market: Long-held 1966 Laurel Grove house lists at $3.295m; charter club perk included
stories.summary: Now available on the market is a charming four-bedroom house in Kentfield, originally constructed in 1966. This midcentury gem has been tastefully renovated, featuring an expansive 2,784 square feet of living area set on a spacious lot. With modernized interiors and exclusive access to a local club, this well-established residence awaits its new owner after nearly sixty years of cherished memories.

stories.title: Cheque-bounce case: Actor Rajpal Yadav seeks exemption from surrender, SC says deposit Rs 5 cr first
'Releasing 6,000 cusecs is impossible': Karnataka on Cauvery water order, may move Supreme Court
stories.summary: Karnataka may approach the Supreme Court regarding water release orders. The Cauvery Water Regulation Committee recommended releasing 6,000 cusecs daily. This recommendation was upheld by the Cauvery Water Management Authority. Karnataka officials cited declining water inflows and drinking water needs. The state government is seriously considering filing a petition soon.

stories.title: Panama City school left empty for years is getting a second life
stories.summary: The former Panama City Grammar School will undergo redevelopment into apartments and townhomes. City officials have cleared financial hurdles, waiving fines and providing a grant for the project. Developer Zachary Seymour will purchase the property and begin necessary structural repairs. The agreement mandates completion of critical repairs within one year to preserve the historic structure. Local leaders emphasize saving heritage, especially after Hurricane Michael's significant damage.

stories.title: No rooms, Rs 2.3 lakh a night: BRICS Summit sends Delhi hotel rates soaring
1,800 years ago, a Roman household decorated floor with cat and dog; archaeologists uncover mosaic
stories.summary: Archaeologists in Turkey have uncovered a colourful Roman-era mosaic dating back around 1,800 years. Found inside a villa at ancient Adramytteion, the mosaic features 15 panels showing animals and mythological figures. Two animals are named in Greek: a cat called Emerald and a dog called Ocean.

stories.title: NCPCR summons Meta India chief over alleged child sexual abuse material ads
ABVP seeks MCD chief’s exit, PG audits after Satya Niketan tragedy
stories.summary: The ABVP has demanded safety audits for paying guest accommodations in student areas. They also called for the Municipal Corporation of Delhi commissioner's resignation following a recent tragedy. Thousands of students participated in a march to highlight safety concerns and hostel shortages. The organization urged Delhi University to build more hostels for students. They seek immediate action and structural checks on unsafe accommodations.

stories.title: India, China hold first high-level military flag talks in Arunachal amid LAC tensions
stories.summary: The meeting followed understandings reached during the Special Representatives dialogue between National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi. The talks are part of efforts by the two countries to maintain peace along the Line of Actual Control and gradually improve bilateral ties. MEA spokesperson said meeting was held at Wacha on the Indian side on September 6 and at Damai on the Chinese side on September 7.

stories.title: Channi vs Warring: Why Sachin Pilot may be Congress's best bet in Punjab
stories.summary: In a strategic move to mend internal discord, Congress appointed Sachin Pilot to lead efforts in Punjab, following Bhupesh Baghel's ousting due to his inability to unify the Channi and Warring factions. With a wealth of experience from Rajasthan, Pilot faces the challenging task of overcoming anti-incumbency against the ruling AAP government. His triumph here may pave the way for a more significant role back in Rajasthan.

stories.title: 'Not intended to hurt anyone': CM Vijay clarifies gesture in TN assembly after DMK protest
California town first sold on eBay in 2002, is back on market again
stories.summary: Bridgeville, an 80-acre town in Northern California, made history in 2002 as the first town to be listed on eBay. The auction drew 250 bids, with the highest reaching $1.77 million, but the winner backed out. After several owners and failed plans, the town is set to return to the market this September, with its current owners hoping for someone who can help the community flourish.

stories.title: As El Niño intensifies, scientists in Chile are making a vulnerable penguin species wear copper vests, here's why
stories.summary: In an inspiring initiative, Chilean researchers are designing specialized vests for injured penguins, incorporating copper and zinc to expedite healing. This groundbreaking effort is focused on supporting the struggling Humboldt penguin population by preventing further injury while enhancing recovery. The vests draw on effective treatments that have proven successful for domestic animals, showcasing a creative blend of technology and compassion.

stories.title: 4 members of Florida family missing after plane vanishes en route from Bahamas to Miami
Texas offers $100 for invasive black carp caught near state waters
stories.summary: Texas offers a hundred-dollar bounty for each invasive black carp caught. This program aims to improve understanding of the species spreading through river systems. Participants can receive up to ten reimbursements monthly for collected specimens. Research focuses on the fish's age, growth, and distribution patterns. Black carp pose a threat to native freshwater mussels and snails.

stories.title: In 1980, conservationists began eradicating feral sheep to restore California's Santa Cruz Island
stories.summary: Conservationists undertook a significant effort to remove feral sheep from Santa Cruz Island, aiming to revive its delicate ecosystem. Over seven years, thousands of these sheep were eliminated, risking the extinction of a unique heritage breed. To counter this, twelve lambs were rescued to spearhead a captive breeding initiative on the mainland, ensuring the preservation of a rare genetic lineage and honoring California's rich agricultural heritage.

stories.title: Digital asset firms seek sovereign funds’ backing at Delhi meet
'Poisonous': Rahul Gandhi targets 'India's most corrupt' MP govt over liquor deaths
Evening News Wrap: Modi-Putin bilateral meet on Friday, gun-carrying man held at PM's Mumbai event, Rijiju slams Rahul
Hidden gut bacteria populations linked to ageing, cancer and type 2 diabetes may spread worldwide
stories.summary: Scientists led by the University of Vienna have found hidden populations within common gut bacteria, some of which are linked to ageing, colorectal cancer, inflammatory bowel disease and type 2 diabetes. The study also found evidence that certain bacterial populations can spread between people and across continents within a few decades, suggesting the gut microbiome may be more transmissible and dynamic than previously thought.

stories.title: Man hid inside a Roman storage jar 1,600 years ago; archaeologists uncover his final moments
stories.summary: Archaeologists have unearthed the skeletal remains of a man tucked inside a massive Roman storage jar, offering a chilling glimpse into the past. It appears he sought refuge from a violent raid, as evidenced by the surrounding destruction and signs of fire. Two iron knives discovered alongside him imply a desperate act of self-defense. This city's fate remained enigmatic for an astonishing sixteen centuries before it was eventually rebuilt.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Bruce Lee: "If you always put limits on everything you do, physical or anything else, it will…"
PM Modi holds four-hour review meeting with 20 ministers on governance, welfare
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi held a four-hour review meeting with ministers. He focused on key government initiatives and their implementation on the ground. Ministers presented progress reports on their respective departmental work. Actionable ideas were sought for a developed India vision by 2047. PM Modi stressed digital engagement and plans more such sessions.

stories.title: 'Rumours of mobile jammers at Satya Niketan site false': Delhi Police reacts to AAP's allegations
Former mayor Giuliani says Mamdani should skip New York’s 9/11 memorial ceremony
At 13, a UK boy’s plant-selling business helps pay his £4,000 school fees
Indian envoy meets Bangladesh president, stresses strengthening 'deep-rooted' ties
Why is N3on becoming an AI streamer? Kick star defends controversial never-ending livestream
stories.summary: On September 7, 2026, Kick streamer N3on unveiled a groundbreaking AI streaming initiative that aims to make him the first AI streamer with an uninterrupted broadcast. This pioneering project is designed to operate continuously, even when N3on is offline. He positions this venture as an exciting evolution in content creation while reassuring fans that his traditional streaming will persist alongside this new experiment.

stories.title: SC to consider Satya Niketan case transfer from Delhi HC over PG building collapse
stories.summary: A bench of Justices Ahsanuddin Amanullah and R Mahadevan was hearing a plea seeking urgent intervention after the building housing a boys' paying guest accommodation collapsed near Delhi University's South Campus. Seven students were killed and five others were injured. The court noted that the Delhi high court was already dealing with the incident but said the issues raised appeared to overlap with a broader case before the Supreme Court

stories.title: TN Assembly passes resolution urging Centre to use official OBC names in 2027 Census
stories.summary: The resolution covers Backward Classes, Most Backward Classes and Denotified Communities listed by the Tamil Nadu and Union governments. It also calls for these official lists to be built into the census portal so that people can select their caste from a fixed list rather than enter names themselves. The resolution said caste details should be collected for these communities in the same manner as data for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

stories.title: New York is building a bridge with recycled glass: $21.2 million project to divert 106 tons of glass from landfills and prevent over 72 tons of CO2 emissions
stories.summary: A New York bridge initiative is making headlines by incorporating recycled glass into its concrete mix. This project effectively diverts waste glass from landfills, significantly cutting down on carbon emissions. By transforming unwanted glass into a sustainable alternative for cement, this pilot demonstrates forward-thinking in construction materials. The expected completion of the project, including accompanying sidewalks, is slated for late 2026.

stories.title: Why Harry and Meghan were caught off guard by King Charles’ latest letter
stories.summary: King Charles III has clarified Prince Harry and Meghan's status as private citizens. The royal family confirmed they remain non-working members, which was previously agreed. This clarification came shortly before a letter was sent to senior officials. Harry and Meghan continue their commercial and charitable work in their private capacity. Their security arrangements remain a separate and ongoing discussion.

stories.title: 3 held for entering Mumbai mall with firearm; police rule out link to PM Modi event
Terror conspiracy case: NIA chargesheets US citizen, 6 Ukrainians for training anti-India forces
The couple who saved The African Queen now own a £3.9m Scottish castle
stories.summary: An American couple has purchased Carbisdale Castle in Scotland. They plan to transform parts of the historic property into a boutique hotel. This venture follows their successful restoration of the famous African Queen steam launch. The castle, once known as the 'Castle of Spite,' will offer short-term stays initially. Their vision includes creating a unique Scottish hospitality experience for guests.

stories.title: Wales turns 80,000 used nappies into road-surfacing material
Rare Cong-BJP unity in Bengal over Bageshwar Baba's Durga Puja meat diktat
15 Indian-origin men charged in Canada extortion probe; police release photos
Robin Williams’ 640-acre Napa estate sold for $18.1M after a $35M listing
Shakespeare’s Globe to replace 30-year-old roof with 14,000 reed bundles in £10m project
stories.summary: Shakespeare’s Globe in London is set for a major roof replacement nearly 30 years after the reconstructed theatre opened. The £10 million project will use traditional thatching and around 14,000 bundles of reed instead of modern roofing materials. The Globe’s original roof used 6,000 bundles of Norfolk reeds. The project comes as traditional thatching in England faces challenges including poor harvests, old machinery and uncertain seasonal labour supplies.

stories.title: She built a 12-by-12-foot cabin with no electricity or road: The woman who chose to live alone in the Adirondack wilderness
stories.summary: Anne LaBastille, an iconic figure in wilderness living, constructed a secluded cabin in the Adirondack wilderness, eschewing all modern perks. Her life there was immortalized in her famous 'Woodswoman' memoir series, capturing the essence of nature. Later, her beloved property was turned over to New York State for conservation, now part of the Forest Preserve, showcasing her lasting impact in inspiring nature lovers and protecting the great outdoors.

stories.title: 'Why bring BJP into this?' Rijiju slams Rahul for targeting Shah over Manipuri musician's murder
Quote of the day by Fyodor Dostoevsky: "Your worst sin is that you have destroyed and…"
Over 100 eagle rays gather off Malta in largest aggregation ever recorded
Satya Niketan tragedy: ABVP seeks PG safety audit, MCD chief’s suspension
PM Modi-Putin talks: 5th gen Su-57s, nuclear power plants & US sanctions on agenda
'Turned quiet life into chaos': Virginia man sues Amazon over data centre
IISc’s FSID appoints first industry leader as CEO under new model
stories.summary: The Indian Institute of Science's FSID has appointed Omprakash Subbarao as its new CEO, signaling a pivotal transition to an industry-driven governance structure. With aspirations to evolve into a self-sustaining entity, FSID aims to spur innovation and incubation by undertaking a thousand industry initiatives and fostering three hundred deep-tech startups, while enhancing collaboration with corporations and MSMEs for tangible outcomes.

stories.title: Japan’s floating solar farm faced Typhoon Faxai; modules broke loose and 50 panels caught fire
stories.summary: In 2019, a severe typhoon struck Japan's largest floating solar farm, leaving it heavily damaged. This event highlighted the engineering flaws present in floating solar structures when confronted with extreme weather. Investigators identified anchor failures as the main factor contributing to the significant damage. In response, the project was restructured into smaller, more resilient floating modules. Now, it serves as a reference for enhancing solar technology's storm resilience.

stories.title: Bengaluru start up gets US patent for its satellite imaging tech
Dubai teen built AI platform for breast cancer after losing grandmother at 10; took cancer awareness to India
stories.summary: Saiyette Aima’s journey began with her grandmother’s battle against breast cancer, driving her to make a significant impact. She spearheaded community-oriented fundraising and awareness campaigns, which flourished with local backing. Following this, Aima launched Pink for Purpose and started a YouTube channel to enhance her outreach. Her mission extended to India, providing free screening camps, which culminated in the innovative CareCheck, an AI tool for guiding breast health decisions.

stories.title: Another French museum heist: Thieves steal 4 paintings worth Rs 93 cr from Renoir museum; drop one while fleeing
ED detects Rs 60 crore ‘irregularities’ after 24-hour search at TMC MP Nadimul Haque’s premises
As 9/11 attacks collapsed his office, a blind man's guide dog helped him down 78 flights to safety
stories.summary: During the harrowing 9/11 attacks, Michael Hingson's guide dog, Roselle, became his lifeline, leading him down seventy-eight floors from the north tower. Together with his colleague David Frank, they managed to escape the crumbling World Trade Center amid chaos. While firefighters bravely climbed upward, Hingson and Frank made their way to safety. In the aftermath, Hingson found solace through sharing their powerful story of trust and collaboration.

stories.title: Mozart's melodies were less predictable, teen finds
stories.summary: Eighteen-year-old Linus Chen-Plotkin from Philadelphia has created a groundbreaking study on the genius of Mozart. Using statistical tests to evaluate melody predictability, he found that Mozart's music demonstrated significantly lower predictability than that of his contemporaries. This unique characteristic allowed him to both adhere to classical standards and surprise his audience, offering fresh insights into the nature of musical innovation and the essence of artistic excellence.

stories.title: Japan installs playful signs warning drivers about cats on the road
Meet Celine Zhang, 18, who can prove puzzles without revealing answers
Toronto uses cold water from 83m beneath Lake Ontario to cool 200 buildings across downtown
stories.summary: In a bold move towards sustainability, Toronto harnesses the icy depths of Lake Ontario for its cooling systems. By drawing from eighty-three meters beneath the lake's surface, this network services two hundred buildings and spans over forty million square feet. This innovative strategy not only slashes electricity usage compared to traditional AC methods but also revamps a natural asset into core urban infrastructure.

stories.title: 'Some can never be happy with India's progress': PM Modi renews 'naraz fufa' jibe at Congress in Vadodara
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated development projects worth over thirty-five thousand crore rupees in Vadodara. He highlighted the successful completion of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor sections connecting key industrial hubs. The Prime Minister also criticised previous governments for significant delays in executing the freight corridor project and emphasised the transformation in the nation's work culture and logistics system since 2014.

stories.title: 'Character assassination must stop': Kangana slams targeting of Tamil Nadu actress 'for her relations'
'To stop love jihad': Maharashtra minister Nitesh Rane backs VHP's call to bar Muslims from Navratri events
Mississippi teen who wrote an autism book for her sister finishes second at Miss America’s Teen
stories.summary: Mississippi teen Madalyn Sullivan has finished as first runner-up at Miss America’s Teen after representing her state at the national competition. An Oxford High School student, Sullivan founded Millie’s Mission, an initiative inspired by her sister’s autism diagnosis. She also co-authored the children’s book “Meet Millie” and donated copies to public libraries across all 82 Mississippi counties.

stories.title: 'Every Northeast family in Delhi asking - are we safe?' Rahul on Manipuri musician's killing
Fired after 15 years on Wall Street, Bloomberg turned $10M into $109B and gave away $25.4B
DMK MLAs evicted from TN assembly after ruckus over CM Vijay's remarks
‘Forgotten who Delhi belonged to’: Hafiz Saeed’s son threatens India in jihadist speech
Robot finds rare bigfin squid two miles below California in first live Northeast Pacific sighting
Dam Removal Reopens Habitat: Virginia project reconnects 127 miles; migratory fish return upstream
stories.summary: In 2014, the removal of Harvell Dam revitalized over 120 miles of river, providing essential upstream habitats for migratory fish. Observations from state biologists and anglers confirmed fish migrating upstream post-demolition. This collaborative restoration project united various agencies and organizations, successfully restoring the river's free-flowing state and enhancing benefits for both aquatic life and recreational activities.

stories.title: Six people buried in a rare Viking Age grave reveal violence, family ties, and Baltic ancestry

stories.title: Taiwan faces alarming Chinese presence around its territory
stories.summary: Taiwan reported significant Chinese military incursions around its territory on Saturday. Up to twenty Chinese aircraft and several naval vessels were detected by Taiwan's defense ministry. Many of these aircraft crossed the median line into Taiwan's air defense zone. This surge follows recent days of increased Chinese naval and air presence. Taiwan's Coast Guard Administration noted a substantial rise in Chinese vessels last month.

stories.title: Output overdrive: 30% productivity boost could power 35% of future manufacturing

Leveraging digital solutions and cultivating a positive workplace culture will be essential for driving productivity forward.

In 2018, a Hawaii study found green roofs stayed cooler than white roofs in Honolulu
stories.summary: A University of Hawaii study found green roofs stayed cooler than white roofs. The green roof's average daytime surface temperature was 4.1°F lower. Peak temperatures on the green roof were 18.5°F lower than the white roof. Evapotranspiration from plants cooled the surrounding air significantly. This vegetation offers a method to combat urban heat island effects.

stories.title: Historic Mansion For Sale: 16-room Victorian home hits market; five generations leave legacy
stories.summary: Nestled in Parkersburg, West Virginia, a breathtaking 19th-century mansion known as Chancellor House is on the market. This remarkable estate has been cherished by the same family for five generations since its construction in 1878, showcasing the opulence of its original owner, William Nelson Chancellor. stories.title: Five EU countries move towards first ‘return hub’ for rejected asylum seekers
stories.summary: Five European Union nations are planning migrant return hubs outside the EU. These facilities aim to process rejected asylum seekers for repatriation. stories.summary: A living shoreline project in New Smyrna Beach largely survived Hurricane Matthew's severe winds. This natural approach used vegetation and sand to stabilize the coast effectively. Conventional hardened structures nearby experienced significant damage and erosion during the storm. The project demonstrated how natural defenses can withstand powerful hurricane conditions. This resilience offers a promising model for future coastal protection strategies.

stories.summary: In an inspiring initiative, Nigerian engineer Yahaya Ahmed is turning discarded plastic bottles into sustainable building materials. By filling empty bottles with sand, Ahmed effectively combats plastic waste while providing cost-effective and durable housing alternatives.

stories.title: Gateway of Arch is going dark this September; the surprising reason has everything to do with millions of birds
stories.summary: This September, the Gateway Arch in St Louis plans to turn off its lights in a bid to protect migratory birds heading south along the Mississippi Flyway. This essential route is vital for various bird species. To assist, people can keep their cats indoors, reduce outdoor lighting, and regularly clean bird feeders to help curb the spread of diseases.

stories.title: North Carolina father to spend $800,000 building housing community for disabled son and those like him
stories.summary: Dave Curro is spearheading the development of Forest Grove, an innovative community designed specifically for adults with special needs. This initiative will include 20 tiny homes and a supporting community center, providing essential resources. A recent festival raised significant funds, demonstrating strong community support. stories.summary: Australia’s endangered eastern quolls are showing signs of recovery after conservationists successfully bred captive-raised animals in Tasmania. This vacant California lot is now a refuge from heat waves
stories.summary: In San Ysidro, California, the newly opened La Semilla Community Resiliency Center stands as a vital resource for local residents confronting climate adversity. This innovative center provides essential cooling during sweltering heat and electricity during power failures. Furthermore, it focuses on educating the community about disaster preparedness and sustainable practices, directly tackling critical environmental problems such as pollution and extreme weather conditions.

stories.title: Fire-damaged 1867 Michigan school reborn as a $175,000 public park
Baltimore shopping centre rebounds as 200 community investors take ownership, with 10 new leases and 100+ jobs
stories.summary: Edmondson Village Shopping Center is undergoing a significant transformation driven by local residents. Two hundred community investors now hold a direct ownership stake in the property. Ten new leases have been signed, bringing essential services to the neighborhood. A planned headquarters for Meals on Wheels will create over one hundred jobs. This community ownership model connects residents to the property's economic revival.

stories.title: Meet Kiran Reddy, 18-year-old Georgia teen who became the first Indian American to win Miss Teen USA
stories.summary: Kiran Reddy has made an outstanding mark as the first Indian American crowned Miss Teen USA. Having previously claimed the Miss Georgia Teen USA title, she is celebrated as Georgia's first national winner. A dedicated pre-medical student, Reddy aspires to inspire young girls. She is set to represent the United States at the Miss Teen Universe contest, alongside continuing her academic journey.

Streamer MoistCr1TiKaL drops first look at Godslap animated movie coming in 2028
stories.summary: MoistCr1TiKaL has just announced the Godslap animated movie, a captivating adaptation of his graphic novel. This exciting hand-drawn 2D animation project is produced by Lyrical Animation and Meatier Productions, with animation expertly crafted by Powerhouse Animation Studios, famous for their work on Castlevania. Set in a cyberpunk universe, the plot centers around a young hero taking on a formidable corporation. Production is already underway, targeting a 2028 release.

stories.title: Oakland woman lost $12,145 after scammers posed as Charles Schwab security
stories.summary: An Oakland woman says scammers posing as Charles Schwab security drained her entire $12,145 investment account after a frantic phone call. She denies sharing any information, while Schwab said its investigation found that a verification code was provided to a third party. She is now taking the case to arbitration and has contacted police and the FBI.

How a stranger's advice helped Tiffany Haddish go from living in her car to bying 17 properties
stories.summary: Tiffany Haddish went from experiencing homelessness and living on a $500-a-month budget to building a real estate portfolio of about 17 properties. She credits advice from an accountant she met during a trip to China and Japan for changing her approach to money. She also used acting pay cheques to buy and pay off property.

Former Ravens coach John Harbaugh's 1905 Maryland stone mansion sells for $6M
stories.summary: Former Baltimore Ravens coach John Harbaugh has sold his historic stone mansion in Owings Mills, Maryland, for $6 million. He bought the 9-acre property for $3 million in 2013. Built in 1905, the 9,100-square-foot home has five bedrooms, a carriage house, four-car garage, pool, hot tub and multiple outdoor spaces.

Rahul Gandhi vs C Joseph Vijay: Can TVK chief do what Arvind Kejriwal could not?
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu's chief minister Vijay faces a political challenge regarding national leadership. His party, TVK, and the Congress coalition are debating the 2029 prime ministerial candidate. Vijay's rise disrupts traditional state politics and sparks national aspirations. He must balance state leadership with a broader political project. This dynamic creates tension within the ruling coalition. Is he ready to have a direct contest with Rahul Gandhi?

stories.title: Three women survived a deadly Grand Canyon flood after clinging to a rock ledge for 5 hours
stories.summary: Three women survived a dangerous flash flood in the Grand Canyon. They clung to a rock ledge for five hours while debris swept past. Separated briefly, each feared the others had been lost to the waters. A rescue helicopter eventually spotted the stranded hikers and brought them to safety. This survival occurred during a larger disaster which claimed other lives.

stories.title: Russian strike damages WHO warehouse in Ukraine; second such attack in weeks
The story of Tsutomu Yamaguchi, the only survivor of both Hiroshima and Nagasaki atomic bombings
stories.summary: Tsutomu Yamaguchi's remarkable story is one of survival against unimaginable odds, as he endured the horrors of two atomic bombings just days apart in August 1945. Initially in Hiroshima on August 6, he found himself in Nagasaki on August 9. Post-war, Yamaguchi channeled his experiences into activism, passionately advocating for nuclear disarmament at the United Nations, illustrating the catastrophic effects of nuclear armament.

stories.title: A giant 10-sided wave is emerging around Saturn’s south pole, Hubble observations show
stories.summary: Saturn's south pole reveals a giant, evolving 10-sided atmospheric wave. Hubble telescope observations trace subtle signs of this pattern back to 2023. This newly identified feature is embedded in a powerful jet stream and extends through multiple atmospheric layers. Scientists have searched for a southern counterpart to the northern hexagon for decades. This discovery offers a rare chance to observe a major atmospheric pattern developing in real time.

stories.title: A $5.5M Portland power project could remove 400 trees from Forest Park while powering over 55,000 homes; the deal has split conservation groups
stories.summary: Amidst rising concerns, Portland General Electric's tree-removal project has drawn fervent opposition from conservationists who fear for the health of mature forests and wildlife. While the utility argues that this initiative is crucial for ensuring consistent power to households, the city is in the process of evaluating a new application and awaiting feedback from the staff. The decision will ultimately balance environmental impacts with the necessity of electrical reliability.

stories.title: Tech entrepreneur's Martha's Vineyard estate bought for $19 million sells for record $43 million
stories.summary: A 31.59-acre estate in Edgartown on Martha’s Vineyard has sold for a record $43 million. Tech entrepreneur Michael Bronner spent $19.125 million between 2019 and 2023 assembling the property, which includes an 8,994-square-foot, 12-bedroom home. The sale surpassed both the island’s previous $37.5 million record and Massachusetts’ $38.1 million record.

stories.title: Indian-origin London cop Prakash Patel charged with 5 counts of sexual assault
stories.summary: A detective sergeant in London has been charged with five sexual assault offenses involving four women he is familiar with. Following his arrest last April, he was suspended from his position. The Crown Prosecution Service has authorized these charges after a thorough investigation carried out by the Metropolitan Police's professional standards teams.

Seatbelt sign off, hydraulic failure, pilot tests positive for psychoactive substance: What Air India Phuket probe found
stories.summary: An Air India flight faced serious challenges with multiple hydraulic failures and altitude disturbances. Following the incident, the pilot-in-command tested non-negative for psycho-active substances. Passengers sustained injuries, and the aircraft suffered considerable cabin damage. After evaluating the situation, the crew chose to proceed to Delhi. The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau is diligently examining all aspects of this alarming event.

Scientists reveal 7 countries most likely to survive a global collapse by maintaining society and food production
stories.summary: In an intriguing analysis, two studies have spotlighted seven island nations poised to withstand global calamities. New Zealand emerges as the frontrunner, lauded for its geographic isolation and abundant local resources. Australia, on the other hand, shines in nuclear winter scenarios, showcasing its vast food production potential. Both countries, however, grapple with import dependency for vital supplies, indicating distinct variations in their readiness based on various global crisis models.

stories.title: US House passes bill to stop federal funding of universities boycotting Israel
stories.summary: The US House has approved a bill aimed at halting federal support for universities that boycott Israel, marking a significant political shift that now awaits Senate approval. The vote reflected a mostly partisan divide, with some Democrats voicing concerns about free speech implications. Amid escalating protests against Israel's actions in Gaza, supporters assert that the legislation addresses antisemitism, a claim contested by demonstrators who disagree with its intent.

IndiGo aircraft hits parking stand pole at Srinagar airport
stories.summary: An IndiGo flight had a minor mishap upon landing in Srinagar, coming into contact with a parking stand pole. Fortunately, all passengers and crew deboarded without issue. Authorities have been alerted, and an investigation is currently in progress. The aircraft involved will undergo necessary maintenance and will return to service once it passes all required inspections.

In 2023, Princeton researchers tested radiative cooling, keeping a building 3.9°C cooler
stories.summary: Researchers tested a building's ability to stay cooler than outside air naturally. A special roof released heat towards the sky, while airflow moved air through openings. This passive system kept the test box significantly cooler than the prevailing outdoor temperature. The experiment demonstrated radiative cooling working with thermal mass and temperature-driven ventilation. This approach offers a way to cool buildings without mechanical systems.

stories.title: Use of drugs serious concern, act on it quickly, AAIB to DGCA on AI Phuket-Delhi flight interim report
stories.summary: An Air India flight experienced severe turbulence and multiple hydraulic failures. The pilot-in-command tested positive for a psychoactive substance after the incident. This led to an interim safety recommendation from the AAIB to the DGCA. The aircraft suffered significant cabin damage during the extreme turbulence event. Investigations into the technical causes of the hydraulic failure are still ongoing.

stories.title: South Florida teens use pizza and tech to fight hunger, delivering 25,000 slices to food deprived families
stories.summary: Meet a passionate brother and sister team from South Florida who launched Pizza for a Purpose, an app aimed at alleviating hunger. This unique platform unites generous donors, local pizzerias, and community organizations, leading to the distribution of over 25,000 pizza slices to families. Their philanthropic journey also includes establishing the Dhanam Foundation, which aims to expand their outreach and charitable efforts significantly.

stories.title: Illinois businessman built a giant wind chime to attract visitors, then made 12 Guinness records
stories.summary: Jim Bolin transformed struggling Casey, Illinois, with giant attractions. What began with a record-breaking wind chime grew into 21 oversized objects and 12 Guinness World Records titles, drawing visitors and national attention to the small town.

Air India Phuket-Delhi incident: All 3 hydraulic systems failed; pilot tested positive for psychoactive substance
stories.summary: An unsettling incident occurred when an Air India pilot's post-flight drug test returned a non-negative result for a psychoactive substance. This followed a dramatic altitude drop over Odisha, resulting in injuries to twenty passengers and four crew members. The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau has identified this as a serious problem, calling for the Directorate General of Civil Aviation to respond urgently.

Play, deport, repeat: Trump launches arcade-style immigration games
stories.summary: The White House has introduced online games with a "MAGA" theme to promote immigration policies. Players can engage in activities like deporting migrants and building a border wall. One game, Rio Run, features a border official chasing migrants along the Rio Grande. Another game, Build the Wall, involves stacking blocks to construct a border barrier. These games aim to communicate administration policies through entertainment and social media platforms.

Third Phase Restoration: Hidden parquet floors emerge at Hopewell Museum; reopening set for December 2026
stories.summary: The Hopewell Museum is embarking on a remarkable restoration project for its historic house. Careful attention is being given to preserve original elements such as the floors and windows while integrating modern systems to enhance protection of the museum's collections. This comprehensive renovation aims to ensure the building is well-prepared for future use, with a reopening slated for late 2026.

stories.title: 'Profound inspiration for selfless action': PM Modi extends greetings to nation on Janmashtami
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi shared heartfelt Janmashtami greetings with the nation, reflecting on how Lord Krishna's teachings spur selfless deeds and lead humanity towards a brighter future. President Draupadi Murmu echoed these sentiments, urging all Indians to embody Krishna's virtues. In support, Home Affairs Minister Amit Shah hailed Krishna as the symbol of righteousness, while opposition leader Mallikarjun Kharge extended wishes for joy, harmony, and abundance to all.

The rocket precisely placed the 2,367-kg satellite into its intended orbit. ISRO chief V Narayanan confirmed the satellite's good health after injection. This launch adds to India's growing earth observation capabilities.

Michigan farmer protects his family’s 131 acres from future housing development
stories.summary: Michigan farmer John Boyer bought back his family’s 131 acres after the land changed hands over decades. In 2026, he sold its development rights to the Little Traverse Conservancy through a conservation easement, ensuring the property cannot be divided for housing or commercial development. Boyer hopes the farmland remains protected for generations.

Two friends transformed a 225-acre overgrazed Texas ranch, bringing back quail and wildlife
stories.summary: Two friends, Jim Willis and John Webb, bought a 225-acre overgrazed ranch in Texas in 2000 that could support little beyond cattle. They gradually restored native prairie, planted 3,000 sand plum trees, added a five-acre wetland and changed grazing practices. The work transformed the property into habitat for bobwhite quail, grassland birds, deer, ducks and other wildlife, while also encouraging nearby landowners to join a larger habitat corridor project.

Meet Nithya Ravuri, California school student whose nonprofit has grown to more than 500 members
stories.summary: A California high school senior founded Sevah Neuro, a global network for neurodivergent children. This organization provides resources and social connections, growing to over 500 members worldwide. Sevah Neuro offers a summer fellowship program with life skills and social activities for children. The student-led initiative also engages in legislative advocacy for greater awareness and resources. Future plans include developing an educational book, a mobile app, and physical learning centers.

stories.title: In 2002, Idaho buried nearly 300 tons of crushed waste glass beneath Highway 75
stories.summary: Idaho's innovative approach has seen nearly 300 tonnes of waste glass repurposed as road foundation material, addressing both engineering challenges and local waste management issues. The crushed glass cullet, strategically laid beneath a highway section, has proven to be an effective solution, showcasing the potential of recycling in constructing sustainable infrastructure. This project represents a significant advancement in civil engineering practices through resource optimization.

Built in 1906 to carry coal, five West Virginia railroad bridges to be restored for hikers
stories.summary: More than a century after five railroad bridges were built in 1906 to carry coal through West Virginia’s New River Gorge, an $11.8 million project is now restoring them for public use. The work will repair the historic Rend Trail, replace ageing wooden bridge structures, improve safety and accessibility, and reconnect the 3.2-mile trail with nearby community routes. The National Park Service expects the project to take about 16 months, with the full trail expected to reopen next fall.

stories.title: Meet Jonathan Thai, the 17-year-old whose nonprofit raised $30,000, donated 400 bikes
stories.summary: After a local retailer slashed community biking programs, a Georgia teenager took action by founding Pedal Forward. This initiative has successfully raised over thirty thousand dollars, providing four hundred bicycles to children in need. Hundreds have benefited from free cycling skills clinics, and the organization's reach is expanding into Tennessee and New York. Now, Pedal Forward is setting its sights internationally, planning humanitarian efforts in Vietnam.

In 2009, Washington removed a century-old dike and let tides reclaim 762 acres
stories.summary: In 2009, the decision to remove sea dikes from the Nisqually River Delta paved the way for a remarkable transformation, rejuvenating 762 acres of marshland. Young Chinook salmon swiftly adapted to the new tidal channels, fostering their feeding and growth. This comprehensive restoration successfully re-established 21 miles of ancestral tidal channels with Puget Sound, showcasing a promising blueprint for coastal resilience in the West Coast regions.

5 popular streamers Ethan Klein has sued in the past 3 years: iDubbbz, Denims and more
stories.summary: Ethan Klein's legal battles with streamers have taken several turns since 2025. Denims, Kaceytron, Frogan and SeanDaBlack became involved in a copyright dispute surrounding Klein's “Content Nuke: Hasan Piker” video, while iDubbbz faced a separate defamation lawsuit. One case settled, another ended in default, one remains active, and the final lawsuit was dropped after an apology from Jomha.

stories.title: In 2016, conservationists put the bends back into a Lake District river straightened 200 years earlier
stories.summary: Conservationists undertook an inspiring project to restore the natural meanders of Swindale Beck, which had been straightened for centuries. Within just a few months, the restored gravel beds welcomed back the Atlantic salmon to spawn, while also decreasing flood risks and enhancing drinking water quality for millions. This remarkable recovery fostered a thriving habitat for aquatic insects and river birds, ultimately earning the UK River Prize in 2022.

stories.summary: In a bold move, Caio Borralho has issued a challenge to Khamzat Chimaev for a prospective fight, proposing two dates in November and December. After losing his middleweight title, Chimaev is weighing his options. This clash could play a pivotal role in shaping the future of the middleweight division, with Borralho ranked sixth and Chimaev ranked twelfth globally.

In 2020, Ohio removed a dam from the once-polluted Cuyahoga River; it reopened 39 km of habitat
stories.summary: The removal of the Brecksville Diversion Dam has enhanced river habitats, allowing migrating fish to thrive. Researchers documented the arrival of fifteen new fish species within the lower Cuyahoga River. While native species have successfully reestablished their presence, the advent of nonnative species also marked a significant change in the ecosystem. Ongoing efforts to eliminate more dams aim to further rejuvenate the Cuyahoga River basin for future generations.
